summary: Intro discovery focused on model selection for clinical-note summarization and multilingual support. Main blockers: context length (40k+ tokens for long notes), PII concerns and encryption/KMS, and need for tool-calling to access internal EHR APIs. Customer evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; leaning toward Dedicated or Private for data residency and audit controls but wants cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: send pricing/perf spreadsheet, run a benchmark with their prompts, schedule technical deep dive for infra sizing.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-11 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~49 mins | Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lena (Zenith Director ML), Tom (Infra Lead), Priya (CTO), Rogelio (NLP Eng)

[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Wednesday afternoon. Quick intros, I'm Jesse Park, AE at Redwood, with Maya our SE.
[00:12] Maya: Hi all, Maya Singh, I focus on model performance and infra. We'll try to cover both the high-level fit and some technical options.
[00:18] Lena: Hi, Lena here. We're kicking off evaluating LLM infra for our clinical summarization pipeline and some patient-facing multilingual chat.
[00:25] Tom: Tom, infra. I'm mostly curious about network, VPC, and dedicated GPU sizing.
[00:29] Priya: Priya Rao, CTO. Concerned about compliance and auditability. SOC2 is a must.
[00:34] Rogelio: Rogelio, I'll be the day-to-day for the NLP benchmarks.

[01:05] Jesse: Great. High-level, we want to understand your success criteria: latency SLOs, cost targets, context size, and whether you need tool calling against internal APIs. Can you give us the current stack?
[01:20] Lena: Sure. Right now we use a mix: smaller transformer models for feature extraction in-house, some GPT-like third-party APIs for prototyping, but the plan is to centralize. Key point: our clinical notes average 8-12k tokens but some are long — up to 40k tokens for full visit histories. We need summarization that can handle long context or good retrieval + tool support.
[01:45] Maya: Okay, 40k is a critical signal. That pushes us to either context-extended models or a retrieval augmented approach with chunking + KV cache. Are you currently storing notes in a vector DB?
[01:58] Lena: We have a Pinecone instance for embeddings and a long-term S3 store for raw notes.
[02:05] Rogelio: For summarization we prefer a single-pass where possible, but it's OK to chunk if quality holds. Multilingual: ~10% of notes are Spanish, Portuguese, and some Vietnamese. So the base model needs decent multilingual capability.

[02:38] Maya: On the model side, typical options are: hosted open models in our catalog (quantized when possible), dedicated capacity running the same models but with reserved GPUs, or private deployment inside your VPC/on-prem for the strictest control. Each has trade-offs: hosted is fastest to get started, dedicated lowers unit cost and gives isolation, private gives full control but requires more ops.
[02:59] Tom: For private, what's the network topology? Can we run a private control plane and have nodes in our AZ?
[03:07] Jesse: Yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane and nodes in your VPC or on-prem; we also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management.

[03:25] Priya: On compliance — SOC2 and audit logs — can you export per-request logs? We need retention options and redaction for PII.
[03:33] Maya: We support per-request audit logs, configurable retention, and you can choose to redact or not store prompts. Also in Private/Dedicated you can use your KMS. We have a security pack deck (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack-zenith).

[04:05] Rogelio: Back to models — what's in the catalog for long-context and multilingual? Any candidates you recommend?
[04:12] Maya: We have several open model families: Llama 2 variants (with context extensions in some forks), Mistral, Mosaic, and some long-context optimized models like LongForm-Open (3B/7B variants) and models with native 32k+ context windows. We also offer our own tuned variants with better instruction-following and safety layers.
[04:36] Lena: How reliable are those long-context variants vs chunk+retrieve? Quality wise, single-pass over 40k is nice but I've seen hallucinations when it's stretched.
[04:46] Maya: Right — single-pass can work but it's model-dependent. Our rule of thumb: up to 32k with specialized kernels is reasonable; beyond that we either use multi-stage retrieval+compose or offload some state to KV cache/prefix caching. For clinical accuracy, retrieval with verification steps reduces hallucination risk.

[05:20] Tom: Latency concern: end-to-end for patient-facing chat should be under 800ms p95. For batch summarization we can accept higher. How do dedicated nodes help?
[05:33] Maya: Dedicated reserved GPUs let you control batch sizes and latency SLOs — we can pin model variants and tune batching. For strict p95 < 800ms you may need smaller models or optimized kernels on A100/H100 class hardware; we can provide perf profiles. We'll send a bench spreadsheet with tokens/sec and p95 numbers.

[06:01] Rogelio: Tool-calling — we need the model to call internal EHR APIs to fetch structured data (medication lists) and then synthesize. Does Redwood support function or tool calling?
[06:12] Jesse: Yes, we support structured tool-calling and function outputs. You can define allowed tools; in Private you can host tool adapters inside your network so calls never leave the VPC.
[06:25] Priya: That addresses data residency. For hosted, is there a guaranteed zero-data-retention option?
[06:31] Maya: Hosted has options: we can disable request logging and offer short-term ephemeral storage, but for strict compliance we recommend Dedicated with customer-owned keys or Private.

[07:05] Lena: Cost — can you ballpark per 1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated vs private? We're trying to compare to our current third-party spend.
[07:15] Jesse: Ballpark: hosted with our open quantized models might be $0.4–$1 per 1k tokens depending on model and context; dedicated lowers that to ~$0.15–$0.4 with reserved capacity; private is more a fixed infra cost plus oping costs, break-even depends on volume. We'll send concrete ranges in the spreadsheet.

[07:48] Rogelio: Regarding quantization — do we lose clinical accuracy if we go 4-bit or 8-bit? We've seen regressions on entity extraction in aggressive quantization.
[07:58] Maya: Aggressive quantization can affect some tasks. Our Optimize tooling will recommend per-workload quantization profiles. For critical extraction you may want higher-precision models or hybrid approach: unquantized for entity extraction routes, quantized for generation.

[08:32] Tom: For Dedicated sizing — we have peaks around 120 concurrent requests with average 1k tokens / request during business hours. How do we convert that to GPU counts?
[08:44] Maya: We'll need model choice to estimate; rough rule: a single A100 can handle X throughput at Y tokens/sec for model Z. We'll take your concurrency numbers into the sizing calc in the bench sheet. We'll schedule a more focused infra sizing with Alex.

[09:10] Lena: Multilingual — do models need separate fine-tuning or will a single multilingual variant cover Spanish/Portuguese?
[09:18] Maya: Many open models have decent multilingual capabilities; fine-tuning on your domain data helps. For clinically sensitive languages, we sometimes run language-specific QA passes. For Spanish we recommend an eval set to validate summaries.

[09:40] Rogelio: About fallback policies — if a dedicated pool gets saturated, can we route to a hosted instance temporarily?
[09:47] Jesse: Yes, smart routing allows fallback to compatible variants in hosted capacity. You can set policy orders (dedicated -> hosted-low-cost -> hosted-high-availability). Fallback can be region-aware as well.

[10:12] Priya: Security question — SAML SSO and RBAC?
[10:18] Maya: Supported. You can integrate SSO, enforce RBAC roles, and have per-team usage limits.

[10:30] Rogelio: Quality of transcriptions from medical notes — not the meeting transcriptions, but model summarization correctness — how do you measure it?
[10:38] Maya: We recommend prompt-based evals and rouge/clinical-entity precision recall checks. Redwood Optimize ties regressions to prompt sets and alerts for quality drops when rollouts happen.

[11:05] Lena: On the topic of rollouts — can we canary a model change for 5% of traffic and have automatic fallback?
[11:13] Jesse: Yep, canary + automatic rollback on quality regressions is supported.

[11:28] Rogelio: Any gotchas with long-context models and KV cache? I've heard KV cache invalidation can be tricky when working with streaming and tool calls.
[11:38] Maya: Right — KV cache is session-scoped; when you're mixing retrieval + streaming + tool calls you need to manage cache flush points. Our runtime exposes hooks and we can implement prefix caching so frequently used context doesn't recompute KV every time. That reduces latency and cost.

[12:05] Tom: For private deployment, what's the upgrade path? If Redwood pushes runtime updates, do we coordinate?
[12:12] Jesse: For Private, upgrades are coordinated. You control when to apply updates; we provide release notes and can do staged upgrades.

[12:25] Maya: Let's talk about a concrete pilot. Suggested pilot: 2-week benchmark using your sample prompts, run hosted open model + quantized dedicated instance + private (if you want) to compare cost and quality. We'll run p95 latency measurements, ROUGE/clinical metrics, and cost per 1k tokens.

[12:47] Lena: That sounds good. Timeline: we want a procurement decision by end of July. Security review will be done by mid-June.

[13:00] Jesse: Ok we'll get the security pack and pricing sheet over this week. Maya will run the tech-deep-dive and Alex will do the sizing.

[13:14] Rogelio: Quick question — tool-calling security: can we whitelist APIs at the tool adapter layer?
[13:20] Maya: Absolutely. Tool adapters can be network-isolated and only allowed to call specific endpoints. In Private, they never leave the VPC.

[13:35] Tom: One more infra question — do you support HSM integration for key signing?
[13:40] Maya: Yes HSM/KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated with customer-managed keys.

[14:00] Priya: Thanks — this clarifies a lot.

[14:08] Jesse: Final recap: Action items — Jesse send pricing + model perf spreadsheet; Maya schedule tech-deep-dive and bench plan; Rogelio upload prompts. We'll aim to have the bench run next week and security docs to Priya early next week.

[14:30] Priya: Sounds good. We'll aim to review security pack and get back with any follow-ups.

[14:44] Jesse: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links (security pack, bench spreadsheet) and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

[14:55] Meeting ended.

Notes and references: Security pack link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack-zenith; Bench spreadsheet (to be sent): redwood-bench-templates.xlsx; Mentioned model families: Llama 2 forks, Mistral, LongForm-Open; Tools: KV cache/prefix caching, function/tool-calling, KMS/HSM. Transcription artifacts: occasional mis-hearings (eg "kay vee cache" for KV cache), speaker overlap at 11:38-11:40.
